name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-7B
description: 7" 1024x600 MIPI-DSI panel (EK79007) with GT911 touch on an ESP32-P4, an ES8311 speaker codec, a TF card, RS485, CAN and Wi-Fi through its ESP32-C6. Compiled, not yet seen on a board.
verify: Nobody at LCD Wizard has had this board: the export for it compiles and has not been seen on the panel. Pins, the panel's start-up table and its settings are Waveshare's own, from their Arduino examples for this board (EK79007 on two lanes at 1000 Mbps, 52 MHz, hsync 10/160/160, vsync 1/23/12, LCD reset GPIO 33) and their ESP-IDF BSP. The backlight is GPIO 32 and is lit when the pin is LOW; the export dims it with the PWM inverted. The GT911 has no reset or interrupt line and may answer at 0x14 instead of 0x5D; its readings are mirrored on both axes, which the preset undoes. Boards sold now usually carry an ESP32-P4 of revision 3 (Waveshare's own Arduino examples build for it), and a design on this preset starts on it; for a chip before revision 3 (the upload says "revision v1.x"), choose that under Hardware > Board > Chip revision. The TF card (SDMMC, 4-bit), the ES8311 speaker codec (amplifier on GPIO 53), RS485 (TX 27, RX 26, no direction pin) and CAN (TX 22, RX 21, arriving switched off) are in the kit. Wi-Fi is the ESP32-C6 beside the P4, in the kit as the Wi-Fi co-processor on the ESP32 core's own SDIO lines (CLK 18, CMD 19, D0-D3 14-17, reset 54) - Waveshare publish no pins for it, and their own Arduino Wi-Fi example uses those defaults; it has to run ESP-Hosted of the core's release, which the board prints at start (see the README; Waveshare's FAQ flashes the C6 over its own UART). Wi-Fi through it compiles and has not been on a board. Not driven: the two ES7210 microphones, the camera connector and the C6's Bluetooth; ESP-NOW does not go through the C6.
